anomalies.observed: The USB-C CC1 line (J12 pin A5) is tied to GND through C14, a 100 nF unpolarized capacitor (LCSC C1711). The CC2 line (J12 pin B5) is tied to GND through R7, a 5.1 kΩ resistor. No resistor sits on CC1, so the two CC lines are not treated symmetrically.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that both CC1 and CC2 go through 5.1 kΩ pull-downs to GND (R1 and R7) to declare a default USB-C sink. CC1 should therefore have a 5.1 kΩ resistor to GND, not a capacitor.

evidence.quote: USB-C CC1/CC2 pins go through `R1`/`R7` (5.1 kΩ each) to `GND` — the standard CC pull-down value for declaring the port a default (non-PD) USB-C sink.

anomalies.impact: The CC1 pin has no defined pull-down, so the USB-C sink presents an asymmetric and non-standard CC configuration. A compliant source may not negotiate default USB current or may not detect the attachment reliably in one cable orientation, so the 5 V USB input path (IN2 of U5) may behave unpredictably.

parsed.summary: The CC1 pull-down that the specification requires as a 5.1 kΩ resistor is instead a 100 nF capacitor (C14), and no R1 exists, so the USB-C sink configuration is wrong. The other anomalies I checked are either documented in the specification or are standard practice.
